title: Cadence: Error-Bounded Lossy Compression of Demand Time Series with a Time-Series Foundation Model
abstract: arXiv:2609.06008v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: We present Cadence, an error-bounded lossy compressor for numeric time series pairing a 330M-parameter time-series foundation model (Google TimesFM-3) with an adaptive arithmetic coder, guaranteeing $|\hat{x}_t-x_t|\le\tau$ on every sample. One negative result constrains the design space: for lossless coding a foundation model is worth nothing, because bits saved are logarithmic in predictor accuracy, $\Delta b=\log_2(\mathrm{MAE_{old}}/\mathrm{MAE_{new}})$. So the $1.51\times$ advantage TimesFM-3 holds over a 32-tap linear predictor buys 0.60 bits of 20.28, a median gain of +0.03%. Error-bounded coding escapes this at one point: once a forecast lands inside the band the residual index is zero and the sample nearly free. Cadence contributes: (1) an adaptive range coder with context-modelled binarization, beating xz/zstd on real indices by 9.7% (15/15) and reversing a finding from a general-purpose back end; (2) a determinism result --

translated_title: Cadence：基于时间序列基础模型的误差有界需求时间序列有损压缩
translated_abstract: 我们提出了Cadence，一种针对数值时间序列的误差有界有损压缩器，它将一个3.3亿参数的时间序列基础模型（Google TimesFM-3）与自适应算术编码器相结合，保证每个样本满足误差界 $|\hat{x}_t-x_t|\le\tau$。一个负面结果限制了设计空间：对于无损编码，基础模型毫无价值，因为节省的比特数与预测器精度呈对数关系，即 $\Delta b=\log_2(\mathrm{MAE_{old}}/\mathrm{MAE_{new}})$。因此，TimesFM-3 相对于32抽头线性预测器1.51倍的精度优势，仅能在20.28比特中节省0.60比特，中位数增益仅为+0.03%。而误差有界编码在这一点上摆脱了该限制：一旦预测值落入误差带内，残差索引为零，该样本的编码几乎不占成本。Cadence的贡献包括：(1) 一种采用上下文建模二值化的自适应范围编码器，在真实指数数据上比xz/zstd提升9.7%（15/15全胜），并推翻了来自通用压缩后端的一个已有结论；(2) 一个确定性结果——
tldr: Cadence将时间序列基础模型TimesFM-3与自适应范围编码器相结合实现误差有界的有损时间序列压缩，并揭示了一个关键洞察：基础模型在无损编码中因节省比特数与精度呈对数关系而几乎无用，但在误差有界编码中一旦预测落入误差带即可使样本近乎零成本。
en_tdlr: Cadence couples the TimesFM-3 time-series foundation model with an adaptive range coder for error-bounded lossy compression, showing that while foundation models are worthless for lossless coding due to logarithmic bit savings, they make samples nearly free once predictions land inside the error bound.
